shape_summary.interpretation: Rank-spacing coupling is object-level real (P042 z=-14) and is NOT mediated by conductor, bad-prime count, or torsion (slope survives all three stratifications). It IS mediated by spectral density: N(T) unfolding collapses ~75% of the slope. This suggests the rank->spacing_variance coupling is a density-regime feature — higher-rank L-functions have (analytically) more spread-out zeros, so raw zero gaps scale inversely with rank via the analytic-conductor density factor. Under the charter: P051 is the coordinate system that resolves what this feature really is. Consistent with Pattern 8 hypothesis that F011 GUE deficit is also density-regime.
shape_summary.connection_to_F011: F013 and F011 are both density-regime features under this analysis. If sessionC measured F011 GUE deficit at 38% unstratified and 14% post-first-gap (P050), proper N(T) unfolding (P051) should shrink it further. F013 offers a parallel data point: raw rank-spacing slope -0.00467 -> unfolded -0.00121 (~74% reduction). Same order of collapse as F011 pooled->first-gap.
